prompt: Phones download 4,000-pixel hero images and display them at 400 pixels wide.
trap: The issue is bytes per image, not JavaScript.

prompt: A long article loads 40 images up front, though most are far below the fold.
trap: Virtualization is for huge lists; lazy loading suits images.

prompt: Text jumps down as images load, frustrating readers.
tells: Text jumps down as images load
why: Set width and height (or aspect-ratio) so space is reserved.
trap: It's a layout shift from unsized images.

prompt: Product photos are 1 MB PNGs that would be a fraction of the size in a modern format.
The largest image on the homepage loads last because it's lazy-loaded like everything else.
why: Don't lazy-load the hero; mark it high priority (fetchpriority) instead.
trap: Lazy loading is for below-the-fold images.

prompt: Logos look blurry on high-density phone screens.
why: Provide 2x/3x sources or use SVG for logos.
trap: Right-sized means right for the screen density too.

prompt: Product images pop in abruptly after loading, and the page looks empty until then.
why: Use tiny blurred placeholders and reserved space.
trap: It's perceived image loading, not data fetching.

prompt: Editors upload 8 MB originals, and the site needs many sizes and formats without storing each by hand.
why: An image CDN resizes and converts on the fly.
trap: Optimization can happen at request time.
